findings.title: Unbounded Resonance index can globally freeze signal principal
findings.summary: The starting revision admitted an unbounded lifetime sequence of fresh Resonance revenue notifications. At one raw unit of active signal, two exact public schedules can make the monotonic 1e36 revenue-per-signal index overflow before SignalGBX removal burns sGBX and returns GBX.

severity.likelihoodDetail: Negligible but finite and publicly reachable in the EVM model; the required canonical six-decimal USDG throughput is fantastically beyond a plausible real-world supply.

liveness.permanence: permanent in an affected immutable starting-revision deployment
liveness.notes: Live and killed Strategy exits both checkpoint the same global index before receipt burn and GBX return.

confidence.basis: Reproduced through public functions on the canonical Mine, Router, Resonance, SignalGBX, Strategy, and Bribe graph without storage mutation, then exercised with a source-compatible before/after regression.

status.deploymentDisposition: Fresh deployments must use the remediated bytecode and regenerated consumers; release remains blocked.

assets: all GBX escrowed behind outstanding sGBX
accrued Resonance USDG entitlements whose checkpoint requires the overflowing index
unaffectedPaths: Fund redemption by liquid GBX holders

findings.title: Third parties can force away fractional Bribe rewards
findings.summary: In the starting revision, permissionless beneficiary claims let an outsider choose another account's checkpoint cadence. Each checkpoint floors sub-unit accrual and advances the paid index even when zero is credited, so repeated calls can destroy otherwise combinable reward fractions. ADR 0053 remediates that caller authority in the working tree.

severity.likelihoodDetail: Economically plausible for a sufficiently valuable low-decimal reward, although repeated transaction cost can dominate the destroyed value.
severity.reratingRationale: The combined audit internally re-rates CEX-02 Medium because both impact and likelihood are Medium under the sufficiently valuable low-decimal reward precondition.

liveness.class: repeatable reward-entitlement destruction per account and token
liveness.scope: one beneficiary and one Bribe reward token per attack cadence
liveness.permanence: each floored entitlement is permanently lost; future uncheckpointed rewards can still accrue

confidence.basis: A public-function reproduction with two equal raw-unit signalers and a one-raw-unit-per-second stream deterministically demonstrates the loss.

status.deploymentDisposition: Remediated and internally verified in the working tree; independent closure, deployment authorization, and user-fund authorization remain pending.

Bob claims after both seconds and receives one raw unit because his fractions combined before checkpointing.

findings.title: Unknown signal positions are not discoverable from bounded current state
findings.summary: SignalGBX exposes an account's aggregate sGBX balance but the core exposes neither an enumerable Strategy registry nor a per-account current membership set. A scalar exit is finite once a Strategy address is known. Factory-nonce CREATE derivation can recover a finite global candidate set, but its work grows with all Strategy creations and is not a state-growth-independent bounded fallback.

severity.likelihoodDetail: Historical logs, wallet records, and normal indexers usually preserve keys, but the review explicitly requires an exit not to depend on those external discovery aids.

liveness.class: principal exit has no state-growth-independent bounded discovery path
liveness.scope: per account and per unknown position set
liveness.permanence: principal is recoverable if the missing Strategy addresses are later recovered
liveness.notes: This is a discovery blocker, not a canonical balance mismatch or failure of known-key scalar removal.

confidence.qualification: High on the current-state surface; Medium on the practical loss scenario.
confidence.basis: The production core mappings are non-enumerable, while Lens, SDK, subgraph, and invariant harnesses all explicitly assume caller-supplied or test-maintained Strategy keys. StrategyFactory CREATE outputs can be derived from its current nonce, but the scan grows with total global factory history.

status.deploymentDisposition: Open principal-exit requirement: deployment remains blocked under this review until bounded current per-account membership exists. Durable history and factory-nonce scans are mitigations, not closure.

violatedInvariants.description: The only principal exit must not depend on an indexer or historical data.

findings.whyExistingTestsMissed: Lens and SDK tests supplied Strategy keys, while invariant harnesses maintained a test-only Strategy registry; they proved known-key execution while assuming discovery.

assetDisposition.frozen: unknown-position GBX escrow until the missing keys are recovered
assetDisposition.delayed: unbounded when durable records are unavailable and global factory history continues growing

assetDisposition.description: The problem is exit construction and discovery, not a balance mismatch or attacker transfer.

maximumDamage.description: Up to the account's complete escrowed GBX can remain unreachable under the review's no-history and no-indexer exit requirement.

recovery.available: Recover the missing Strategy addresses from durable history, wallet records, logs, or an index and use scalar removals. Alternatively derive all factory CREATE outputs from the current factory nonce and filter candidates through Resonance.
recovery.currentStateOnly: The deterministic nonce scan is finite but O(total factory creations); no state-growth-independent per-account bounded recovery exists in the reviewed architecture.

findings.title: Mine accepts pre-binding tenures that survive canonicalization
findings.summary: An empty Mine slot can be occupied before GBX permanently binds mint authority because the first occupation has no outgoing tenure to settle and therefore does not mint. After handoff, a later replacement mints the complete preserved pre-binding tenure to the attacker.

severity.likelihoodDetail: Permissionless on a publicly visible unbound candidate, but controllable by atomic or private setup and mandatory abandonment of any touched candidate before exposure.

liveness.scope: one or all sixteen Mine slots on an unbound candidate
liveness.permanence: permanent after the contaminated candidate is bound and exposed
liveness.notes: This is dilution and deployment contamination, not post-launch theft of an existing holder's principal.

confidence.basis: A public-function reproduction occupies a real Mine slot before handoff and receives the exact preserved tenure emission after handoff.

status.deploymentDisposition: Every slot must be proven untouched after binding; any contaminated candidate must be abandoned before funding or user exposure.

violatedInvariants.qualification: The finite Mine settlement guarantee assumes a clean, correctly bound candidate.
An exposed pre-binding candidate can retain attacker-selected tenure state across canonicalization.

users: later GBX holders diluted by preserved pre-binding issuance
deployment operators who bind a contaminated candidate
assets: future GBX issuance from up to all sixteen initial tenures
unaffectedPaths: a fresh candidate abandoned before exposure

codeLocations.role: empty-slot occupation does not require GBX minter handoff

prerequisites: A Mine candidate is publicly callable before GBX permanently binds it.

The setup minter calls GBX.setMinter(Mine).
A later caller replaces the slot and Mine mints the full pre-binding tenure to the attacker.

proof.observedResult: One slot occupied before handoff and replaced ten seconds after handoff pays exactly 40 ether GBX to the pre-binding miner.

maximumDamage.description: An attacker can preoccupy all sixteen initial slots and preserve aggregate initial issuance of 64 GBX per second for the entire pre-binding interval. No existing holder's tokens are directly transferred.

findings.title: Rejected: Mine and Fund uint256 horizon requires a timestamp beyond the target client
findings.summary: Foundry can model a timestamp at which Mine arithmetic overflows, but the pinned Robinhood/Nitro client stores header time as uint64. Canonical public issuance is bounded by 64 ether per second, so target-representable time cannot approach the uint256 boundary.

severity.impactDetail: Counterfactual Critical impact only on an EVM host that admits timestamps larger than the target client can encode; severity is not counted because the candidate is rejected.
severity.likelihoodDetail: The pinned target client's block-header timestamp is uint64, while the modeled overflow requires approximately 1.809e57 elapsed seconds.

liveness.permanence: not applicable on the pinned target execution model
liveness.notes: The defensive Foundry boundary is retained, but it does not falsify target-chain exitability.

confidence.basis: Pinned target-client source uses Header.Time uint64 and TIMESTAMP SetUint64. Source review bounds each slot at 4 ether TPS and aggregateTps at 64 ether; the defensive test proves target-maximum uint64 time remains safe before modeling the host-only boundary.

status.deploymentDisposition: Not a deployment blocker. Preserve the target timestamp proof and do not present host-only vm.warp behavior as reachable.

findings.rejectionReason: The required timestamp exceeds uint64, but the pinned target execution client stores block-header time as uint64 and pushes only that value into TIMESTAMP. With aggregateTps <= 64 ether and GBX minting locked to Mine, effective supply remains at most (2^64 - 1) * 64 ether, roughly 9.8e37 below uint256 maximum.

counterfactual GBX redeemers on that host

counterfactualSequence.action: Occupy all sixteen slots at the initial aggregate rate of 64 ether raw GBX per second.
On Foundry's host-only model, advance beyond uint64 to the last second at which total supply plus pending emission fits uint256; effectiveTotalSupply succeeds.
Advance one more second; effectiveTotalSupply reverts with arithmetic panic.
Fund.redeem reverts when it reads the denominator.
Advance to pendingEmission's first-invalid second; pendingEmission and Mine replacement revert with arithmetic panic.

arithmetic.effectiveSupplyQualification: Any nonzero GBX total supply makes effectiveTotalSupply overflow slightly before pendingEmission reaches its standalone bound.

tests.result: passes; target-maximum uint64 timestamp is in range, then the explicitly host-only Foundry model records exact last-valid and first-invalid uint256 boundaries

proof.observedResult: At type(uint64).max timestamp, pending emission and effective supply remain in range. Foundry can then warp beyond the target representation: at that counterfactual last effective-supply second the view succeeds, and one second later it and Fund redemption revert.

findings.whyExistingTestsMissed: Not applicable: this record is rejected. The initial audit model failed to constrain Foundry's timestamp to the target client's uint64 header representation.

assetDisposition.frozen: none on the pinned target execution model
assetDisposition.delayed: none on the pinned target execution model

recovery.afterHorizon: Not applicable on the pinned target client.
recovery.practicalAssessment: The candidate is rejected on target reachability, not merely assigned a low likelihood.

remediation.recommendedTreatment: Retain the defensive test and target uint64 proof; do not change source for a state the target cannot encode.
tradeoffs: Saturation would silently change pending-supply accounting.
An emission halt would change protocol economics.
Modular arithmetic would be unsafe.
Upgrade or migration authority would violate the intended immutable architecture.

findings.title: Signal exits have a finite ERC-5805 block-clock horizon
findings.summary: OpenZeppelin Votes uses a uint48 default block-number clock. Every SignalGBX burn updates voting checkpoints, so once block.number exceeds type(uint48).max, scalar and batched signal removal revert before sGBX burn and GBX return can complete.

severity.impactDetail: Critical only after the explicit physically non-actionable ERC-5805 clock horizon because all SignalGBX principal becomes globally unremovable.
severity.likelihoodDetail: Physically non-actionable; exact Nitro returns the parent-chain number as uint64, so the uint48 boundary is target-representable but approximately 107 million years away at a 12-second parent-block cadence.

liveness.class: eventual global sGBX burn and signal-exit lock
liveness.scope: global after the ERC-5805 block-clock horizon
liveness.permanence: permanent after the chain block number exceeds uint48
liveness.notes: The separate uint208 safe-supply ceiling blocks excessive new minting but does not trap already valid balances before the block-clock horizon.

confidence.basis: An exact boundary test removes signal at type(uint48).max and observes the expected SafeCast revert at the next block while balances and weights roll back atomically. Exact target source proves NUMBER returns a uint64 parent-chain number and has no lower uint48 guard.

status.deploymentDisposition: Document the finite clock horizon and avoid unqualified claims that signal exits work forever.

liveProbes.interpretation: NUMBER returns the parent-chain block counter; ArbSys.arbBlockNumber returns the distinct L2 header number.

violatedInvariants.qualification: violated only after the explicitly accepted physically non-actionable ERC-5805 clock horizon
The uint48 block clock eventually stops every receipt burn and therefore every signal exit.

users: every sGBX holder after the clock horizon
assets: all GBX escrowed behind outstanding sGBX after the clock horizon
unaffectedPaths: Fund redemption by liquid GBX holders
non-voting protocol paths that do not mint or burn SignalGBX

codeLocations.role: all principal exits eventually burn SignalGBX
receipt burn precedes GBX return atomically
delegates mint and burn accounting to ERC20Votes
every mint or burn transfers voting units and enforces the separate uint208 supply ceiling
uses Time.blockNumber as the default uint48 clock
burns push total-supply checkpoints
checkpoint writes call the uint48 clock
downcasts block.number to uint48
reverts once block.number is greater than type(uint48).max

prerequisites: At least one valid SignalGBX position exists.
The target parent-chain block number returned by Nitro's NUMBER hook advances above 281474976710655, which is type(uint48).max.

reachableSequence.action: A user holds one valid SignalGBX unit allocated to a Strategy.
At block type(uint48).max, removeSignal succeeds and returns GBX.
Create another valid one-unit position before crossing the bound.
Advance to block type(uint48).max + 1.
removeSignal reaches ERC20Votes checkpointing; Time.blockNumber downcast reverts and the entire removal rolls back.

poc.result: passes; last-valid block exits and first-invalid block reverts with SafeCastOverflowedUintDowncast while principal state rolls back

proof.observedResult: Removal at the last uint48 block succeeds. At the next block it reverts with the expected SafeCast error; the user retains one sGBX and the paired Bribe retains one signal-weight unit.

findings.whyExistingTestsMissed: Ordinary tests never advanced block.number to the exact uint48 clock boundary and therefore did not exercise the inherited ERC20Votes downcast during the removal burn.

assetDisposition.frozen: all GBX escrowed behind outstanding sGBX after the clock horizon
assetDisposition.permanentlyTrapped: all GBX escrowed behind outstanding sGBX after the clock horizon
assetDisposition.description: No asset transfers to an attacker; all SignalGBX principal becomes globally unremovable.

maximumDamage.description: Every sGBX burn and therefore every scalar or batched signal-principal exit fails, leaving all outstanding escrowed GBX inaccessible through SignalGBX.

recovery.afterHorizon: No recovery exists in the immutable deployment absent chain replacement or a separately deployed successor, neither of which is provided by the protocol.
recovery.practicalAssessment: The horizon is approximately 107 million years away at a 12-second parent-block cadence, but it remains representable inside the target's uint64 NUMBER path.

remediation.recommendedTreatment: Retain the exact boundary regression, document the finite clock horizon, and avoid unqualified perpetuity language.
tradeoffs: Changing the Votes clock or checkpoint architecture is a major compatibility and governance design change.
An already deployed immutable SignalGBX cannot change its clock behavior.
Adding upgrade or migration authority would conflict with the intended immutable core.
remediation.regressionStatus: The last-valid and first-invalid block regression passes and the horizon remains explicitly accepted.

findings.title: Permissionless Strategy checkpoints maximize accepted floor loss
findings.summary: Any caller can checkpoint one Strategy's Resonance revenue. The checkpoint floors its scaled USDG accrual to whole raw units and advances the paid index even when zero is credited, so attacker-selected cadence can destroy otherwise combinable fractional Strategy entitlement.

severity.impactDetail: Protocol USDG yield is destroyed as ownerless Resonance surplus; no signal principal is blocked and no value is transferred to the caller.
severity.likelihoodDetail: Publicly feasible but generally uneconomic under intended six-decimal USDG because each effective target checkpoint destroys less than one raw unit.

liveness.permanence: each floored fractional entitlement is permanently lost; future uncheckpointed intervals can still accrue
liveness.notes: The PoC makes global division exact and isolates the per-Strategy conversion floor.

confidence.basis: Reproduced through canonical SignalGBX, Bribe, ResonanceRouter, and permissionless Resonance public functions without storage mutation.

status.deploymentDisposition: Retain the Low residual and ordinary-floor disclosure. Any scaled-carry remediation requires an ADR, differential accounting proofs, and fresh review.

users: No account principal is affected; Strategy acquisition inventory may receive less Resonance USDG.
assets: fractional USDG otherwise combinable into the target Strategy's whole-unit entitlement

codeLocations.role: permissionless entry point that checkpoints one caller-selected Strategy
floors Strategy accrual and advances its paid index even when the credited whole amount is zero

prerequisites: At least two live Strategies have nonzero active weight.
A Resonance USDG stream is active.
The target Strategy's entitlement during each chosen interval is below one raw USDG unit.

reachableSequence.action: Give two live Strategies one raw signal unit each.
Schedule one raw USDG unit per second; the exact global index increment is 0.5e36 per second.
After one second, an unrelated caller distributes the target; zero is credited and its paid index advances.
After a second second, repeat; another half raw unit is floored to zero.
Distribute the uncheckpointed control Strategy; its two halves combine into one raw USDG unit.

arithmetic.perCheckpointBound: strictly less than one raw USDG unit per effective target checkpoint
arithmetic.qualification: The example is not a universal maximum; cumulative loss is below the number of effective forced target checkpoints in raw units.

poc.result: passes; two forced target checkpoints pay zero and the uncheckpointed control receives one raw USDG

proof.observedResult: The global division is exact, the target receives zero after each attacker-selected half-unit interval, and the control receives one raw unit after two seconds.

findings.whyExistingTestsMissed: Existing tests documented ordinary per-Strategy flooring and permissionless distribution separately, but did not let an unrelated caller adversarially choose a target Strategy's fractional checkpoint cadence.

assetDisposition.delayed: none; the affected fractions are destroyed rather than deferred
assetDisposition.permanentlyTrapped: the rounded USDG remains ownerless Resonance surplus with no Strategy claim
assetDisposition.description: No value is paid to the attacker. Only the target Strategy's otherwise combinable fractional USDG entitlement is lost.

maximumDamage.scope: one target Strategy per attacker-selected checkpoint
maximumDamage.description: Less than one raw USDG unit per effective checkpoint, but up to 100% of the target's otherwise combinable fractional accrual over those intervals.

recovery.afterLoss: Already floored entitlement is unrecoverable and remains surplus.
recovery.futureAccrual: Stopping forced fractional checkpoints allows later intervals to combine into whole raw units.

remediation.recommendedTreatment: Document the cadence risk. If the protocol later rejects it, introduce scaled per-Strategy carry only through a new ADR and independently reviewed differential accounting change.
tradeoffs: Restricting only distributeRevenue is incomplete because signal additions and removals also checkpoint the Strategy.
Scaled carry adds accounting state and changes the expressly accepted no-carry floor semantics.
No remediation is needed to preserve signal principal because this path does not enter or block principal return.
remediation.regressionStatus: The public-function reproduction passes in the focused audit suite.

findings.title: Public complete-basket claims exceed selective Fund redemption
findings.summary: Tracked landing, deck, and web material promises every Fund holding in one transaction, while Fund intentionally pays only caller-selected token addresses and permanently forfeits omitted shares. The deck also presents discount redemption as guaranteed profitable gap closure, which the protocol does not guarantee.

severity.impactDetail: A holder relying on the broad claim can burn GBX and permanently forfeit the complete original pro-rata share of omitted assets; release materials also overstate price-support certainty.
severity.likelihoodDetail: The contradictory claims are repeated in tracked release-facing landing, deck, brief, and web material, although this review did not establish that any surface is published.

liveness.class: release-claim mismatch and unbounded complete-basket realization
liveness.scope: redeemers relying on the complete-basket claim and every omitted Fund asset
liveness.permanence: each omitted share is permanently forfeited after the selected redemption succeeds
liveness.notes: The bounded one-known-token exit remains available. The finding is that release-facing claims exceed that intentional selective path.

confidence.basis: Fund source, permanent omission tests, the supplied arithmetic argument, and repeated tracked product claims directly establish the mismatch.

status.deploymentDisposition: Release remains blocked until the claims are aligned with caller-selected redemption and non-guaranteed arbitrage support, or Fund is redesigned under a separately reviewed ADR.

users: GBX holders who rely on the complete-basket or guaranteed-arbitrage claim when redeeming
assets: the holder's original pro-rata share of every omitted Fund token
unaffectedPaths: caller-selected redemption of known healthy assets

codeLocations.role: defines caller-selected token redemption and permanent forfeiture of omitted shares
promises that a holder walks away with a share of everything inside
promises every holding in one transaction, including illiquid assets
promises the same proportion of every holding in one transaction
promises everything, always-available redemption, guaranteed profitability, and gap closure
uses a complete-basket title beside a note that correctly limits payout to named assets

prerequisites: A holder relies on the tracked complete-basket or guaranteed-arbitrage language.
The holder cannot identify or include every desired Fund asset in one successful transaction, or intentionally omits one without understanding the forfeiture.
The selected redemption succeeds and burns GBX.

reachableSequence.action: Fund holds at least two non-GBX assets and the holder owns fraction f of GBX supply.
The holder burns fraction x while selecting only one asset.
Fund pays the selected asset and retains every omitted asset; the successful burn is final.
The holder's remaining fraction for omitted assets is (f - x) / (1 - x), which is strictly less than f.

arithmetic.qualification: For 0 < x < f < 1, the remaining fraction is strictly below f, so disjoint later burns cannot reproduce the original complete-basket share.

tests.result: passes; the omitted asset remains entirely in Fund and a later holder redeems against the reduced post-burn supply

proof.observedResult: Fund behavior and its regression are consistent with the selective specification; the tracked product claims are not.

findings.whyExistingTestsMissed: Contract tests correctly asserted selective redemption and omission forfeiture, but the initial disposition did not independently compare every release-facing claim to those mechanics.

assetDisposition.diluted: the redeemer's residual fraction of omitted assets is reduced by the successful burn
assetDisposition.frozen: none for a known healthy selected token
assetDisposition.permanentlyTrapped: if the final GBX supply is burned while assets are omitted, those balances can remain in ownerless Fund with no redemption supply
assetDisposition.description: Omitted assets stay in Fund for the post-redemption supply; no attacker receives them, but the redeemer permanently gives up the omitted original share.

maximumDamage.description: Up to the redeemer's complete original pro-rata share of every omitted asset, potentially all omitted backing if the complete remaining GBX supply is burned without selecting it.

recovery.beforeRedemption: Present accurate caller-selected and forfeiture language and require interfaces to enumerate or deliberately acknowledge selected assets.
recovery.afterRedemption: No path restores the burned holder's original omitted fraction.
recovery.release: Correct all tracked claims before publication or redesign Fund under a new independently reviewed ADR.

recommendedChanges: State that holders redeem a pro-rata share of the Fund assets they select and permanently give up omitted shares.
Describe discount arbitrage as possible support, never guaranteed profit or guaranteed convergence.
Add a release-copy gate against unqualified complete-basket, NAV, guaranteed-profit, and guaranteed-gap-closure claims.
remediation.architectureAlternative: If complete-basket redemption is intended, stop and create a new ADR for a bounded registry, pagination, or redemption-receipt design, then re-audit it.
tradeoffs: Copy correction preserves the current registry-free and selective-redemption architecture.
A complete-basket redesign adds state, gas, discovery, migration, and accounting risk.
remediation.regressionStatus: The contract behavior is covered and the full suite passes; no automated release-copy gate exists yet.
